# A grouped block naming a split that sits in the owner's parked credit.
#
# The block names the settling split of the two-line wire and, beside it, the
# split holding money the customer has already paid into a credit lot. Taking
# that one settles this invoice out of currency the owner is owed, leaving the
# credit short with every figure in the book still balancing.
#
# So it is refused — and the grouped spelling is stricter here than the single
# one on purpose: `txn_split_guid:` naming that same split spends the credit
# deliberately, which is the route the ambiguity refusal sends readers down by
# name. A block naming several splits is saying which of them settle this
# record, not choosing which credit to spend.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the lot, with nothing attached.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
